name: Cisco Talos Intelligence Group - Comprehensive Threat Intelligence_ Bitter APT adds Bangladesh to their targets
outline:
Since August 2021, Cisco Talos has observed a targeted espionage campaign conducted by the Bitter APT group (aka T-APT-17), a suspected South Asian threat actor active since 2013. Known for targeting government, energy, and engineering sectors in China, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia, Bitter has now expanded operations to include Bangladesh.

This campaign uses spear-phishing emails aimed at the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) of the Bangladesh police. The emails impersonate official communications and contain malicious RTF or Excel attachments weaponized to exploit Microsoft Office vulnerabilities (CVE-2017-11882, CVE-2018-0798, CVE-2018-0802). When opened, these files execute embedded shellcode using the Microsoft Equation Editor, leading to the download and execution of a custom trojan dubbed “ZxxZ.”

ZxxZ acts as a downloader with remote execution capabilities, masquerading as a Windows Security update. It collects system information, checks for antivirus processes, and communicates with C2 servers via obfuscated HTTP requests. The infrastructure includes domains like helpdesk.autodefragapp[.]com, and C2 redirection via AWS Global Accelerator to hide real server locations.

Emails originate from spoofed Pakistani government addresses and were sent using a vulnerable Zimbra web client setup. The attackers abuse built-in tools like cURL and Windows Task Scheduler to persist and execute payloads.

This campaign highlights Bitter APT’s evolving TTPs, including malware obfuscation, layered delivery mechanisms, and infrastructure evasion. The use of ZxxZ showcases a step forward in their capabilities.

Defensive recommendations include layered endpoint protection, updated detection rules, and robust incident response plans. Cisco tools like Secure Endpoint, Secure Email, and Umbrella offer specific countermeasures for detection and mitigation.
